topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the cancer lecture series and outlines the session's key learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Mutation Sources, Environmental Factors, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the core nature of cancer as an evolutionary disease influenced by intrinsic biological processes, external environmental exposures, and global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Infectious Agents in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how microbial and viral pathogens drive oncogenesis, illustrated through the pathogenesis and epidemiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms through which specific physical radiation and metabolically activated chemical carcinogens cause DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Initiation, Promotion, and Developmental Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammatory microenvironments, and vulnerable developmental windows cooperate with mutagenic initiation to facilitate tumor growth.

topics.label: Methods for Testing and Identifying Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to detect carcinogen exposure and determine carcinogenic risk.
